As the historic yet hyper-modern capital of **England**, it serves as a global hub for finance, culture, politics, and international diplomacy. For decades, CNN has maintained a massive presence in London, using it as the nerve center for its European, Middle Eastern, and African coverage. Located in the heart of the city, CNN’s London bureau operates around the clock. By **Max Foster**, CNN  
Updated 11:42 AM EDT, Thursday, July 3, 2008

**(CNN) —** Prince William, serving as a sub-lieutenant in Britain's Royal Navy, played a direct role in a dramatic high-seas raid that netted more than $80 million worth of cocaine in the Caribbean, defense officials confirmed Thursday.

The 26-year-old royal — known in the military as Sub-Lieutenant Wales — was on board the frigate HMS *Iron Duke* when it intercepted a high-speed boat carrying approximately 900 kilograms (nearly 2,000 pounds) of cocaine in international waters north of Colombia.

According to the Ministry of Defence (MoD), the operation took place late Tuesday night after a maritime patrol aircraft spotted a suspicious "go-fast" vessel traveling along a known drug-trafficking route. 

The HMS *Iron Duke* launched its Lynx helicopter and a team of Royal Marines in rigid inflatable boats to conduct the intercept under the cover of darkness.

"Sub-Lieutenant Wales was a fully integrated member of the crew and participated in the operation alongside his shipmates," a spokesperson for the Ministry of Defence said in a statement. "He was involved in the tactical planning and execution of the surveillance phase of the boarding operation."

### A high-speed pursuit

Military officials said the crew of the speedboat attempted to jettison several bales of drugs overboard when they realized they were being pursued. Royal Navy personnel launched a quick-reaction boat to recover the cargo while the Lynx helicopter pinned down the target vessel.

Four suspected smugglers were taken into custody by the crew of the HMS *Iron Duke* without casualty. 

"This was a textbook operation," said Commander John Armstrong, the captain of the HMS *Iron Duke*. "The crew reacted swiftly and professionally, and Sub-Lieutenant Wales performed his duties with the utmost diligence, just like any other officer on this ship."

Defense experts estimate the street value of the seized cocaine to be around $80 million (£40 million). Officials believe the shipment was destined for distribution in Europe or North America.

### Royal military training

The operation comes midway through Prince William's five-week deployment with the Royal Navy, a key segment of his intensive military training designed to prepare him for his future role as head of the British armed forces. 

The second-in-line to the British throne has already completed attachments with the British Army's Household Cavalry and the Royal Air Force, where he earned his wings as a pilot earlier this year.

Spokespersons for Clarence House, the Prince's official residence, said William was "thrilled" to have contributed to a successful operation.

"The Prince is gaining invaluable real-world experience during this deployment," a Clarence House spokesperson said. "He is treated no differently than his fellow officers, and he would not have it any other way."

The seized narcotics and the four suspects are expected to be handed over to U.S. law enforcement authorities in the coming days as part of a joint anti-narcotics task force operating in the region.

The HMS *Iron Duke* is currently assigned to the Caribbean to conduct routine counter-narcotics patrols and provide humanitarian relief during the Atlantic hurricane season.
